draft.title: Profit
card: Revenue is the money a business earns from selling its goods or services. Expenses are the costs of running the business, such as wages, rent and stock.
Profit = revenue - expenses. If revenue is more than expenses, the business makes a profit.
If expenses are more than revenue, the business makes a loss. A business that keeps making a loss may not be able to carry on.
Profit rewards owners for the risk they take in putting money into the business. It also pays for growth, such as new equipment or a second shop.
draft.remember: Profit is what is left after expenses are taken from revenue. It rewards risk and pays for growth.

a.q: Last month a bakery earned $9,000 from sales and had $9,800 in expenses. What was the result?
a.why: Revenue minus expenses is $9,000 - $9,800 = -$800, so expenses were more than revenue and the bakery made a loss. A profit of $800 reverses the subtraction.
a.clue: Take expenses away from revenue and check the sign.

b.q: Priya owns a bike repair shop in Bathurst. Her revenue rose this year, but she still made a loss. What must be true?
opts: Her expenses were more than her revenue
Her revenue was less than last year's revenue
Her expenses were less than her revenue
She had no expenses to pay
b.why: A loss happens whenever expenses are more than revenue, however much revenue has risen. Higher revenue only gives a profit if expenses stay below it, so the tempting idea that rising sales mean profit is wrong.
b.clue: A loss depends on how revenue compares with expenses, not on whether revenue rose.

b.best: Her expenses were more than her revenue

problems.detail: The clue 'A loss depends on how revenue compares with expenses, not on whether revenue rose' points straight at the comparison the answer turns on, so it gives the answer away.
